newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark gathers steam for next push up.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark gathers steam for next push up.

text.p: The dollar camped in the middle of it's overnight range against the mark, gathering strength for another push higher in its trek towards 1.75 marks, technical analysts said on Wednesday.
The greenback held above 1.68 marks for most of the U.S. session after falling from a fresh 34-month high at 1.6935 marks in Europe to an overnight low of 1.6740 marks.

Technical analysts expect dollar/mark to once again challenge Wednesday's overnight peak this week, especially after it moved through resistance at 1.6863/68 marks to a U.S. session high in late trade.
Longer-term, a breech of a hefty barrier at 1.71 marks would bode well for a move to the 1.75 target.
"I'm still bullish, even though the price movement overnight was fairly ridiculous," said Randolph Donney, technical analyst at Pegasus Econometric Group.
"I like the way dollar/mark came back and rebounded. Now it is all systems go to the upside," he added.
Dollar near-term support was cited at 1.6755 marks, followed by a sturdy floor at 1.6710 marks.
Meanwhile, the dollar remained mired between the overnight high and low of 124.45 and 123.40 yen, respectively, with a test of the upside expected.
Resistance lies at Friday's four-year high of 124.72 yen and afterward, the 125.00 to 125.20 zone, said a chartist at an investment bank in New York.
Donney said 128.60 remains the major, long-term objective.

The Swiss franc eased against the dollar as the weak Swiss economy continued to weigh on the currency. The related rise in dollar/Swiss could help propell the U.S. unit higher against the mark as well, technicians said.
"Dollar/Swiss seems to be holding above previous daily highs, which is a fairly good omen. We could see dollar/Swiss lead the way," Donney said.
